primary_task: Create a new experiment or tutorial Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) scaffolded from the bundled template with the helper script new_notebook.py and filled with small runnable steps.

requirements.name: python3
requirements.evidence: uv run --python 3.12 python "$JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI" ... ; "The bundled scaffold script uses only the Python standard library and does not require extra dependencies."
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts" (Python is standard software of Linux; also obtainable via apt from Ubuntu)

requirements.name: uv
requirements.evidence: "Prefer `uv` for dependency management." and the example commands `uv run --python 3.12 python "$JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI"`; the script itself can run with plain python ("uses only the Python standard library")
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)" (uv is on PyPI)

requirements.name: bundled skill files (scripts/new_notebook.py, assets/*-template.ipynb)
requirements.evidence: "Use the helper script to avoid hand-authoring raw notebook JSON." ; "Templates live in `assets/experiment-template.ipynb` and `assets/tutorial-template.ipynb`." ; JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI="$CODEX_HOME/skills/jupyter-notebook/scripts/new_notebook.py"
requirements.basis: "skill": "load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins" (the manifest does not say whether this skill's bundled files are installed, nor at the $CODEX_HOME path; check that the skill folder exists in the session)

requirements.name: jupyterlab / ipykernel
requirements.evidence: "Optional Python packages for local notebook execution: uv pip install jupyterlab ipykernel" ; "Run the notebook top-to-bottom when the environment allows. If execution is not possible, say so explicitly"
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)"

notes: Unknown: whether the bundled scripts/new_notebook.py and template notebooks are present (path is under $CODEX_HOME/skills, a Codex layout). If they are absent the agent could hand-write the .ipynb JSON (the document says to prefer the script, and allows raw JSON edits after reading references/notebook-structure.md), so I did not treat absence as unavailable. `uv run --python 3.12` may download a Python build from GitHub releases, which are on the allow-list. Executing the notebook is conditional ("when the environment allows") and not part of the core deliverable.
